posts.author: Pianomaxx
posts.content_md:
Hello Holographers,

I improved my skills in the simple Reflection Holography, and recorded this Holo of an own "sculpture". These are a little play with words: Scales with tones on it, and i tried to mask the tone-holders to make the tones "float", but black paint didnt obviously work so perfect.

The depth is quite impressive in the real holo, as I used a mirror to extend the stairs about 10cm to the back.

![Image](http://www.kingservants.de/x/scales.jpg)

posts.author: Pianomaxx
posts.content_md:
Hi John,

thanks for encouraging me! Of course, I cant compete with all the beautiful, crystal-clear holograms posted in the Gallery, not YET, but I read that many holographers had problems in getting bright Denisyuks on PFG-01 in the beginning. So I keep trying, experimenting, using different chemicals, maybe different plates. But even cutting-edge technology alone can't produce a hologram if you dont know how.

Regarding this, I feel that the most important thing in Holography is not the result, but the growing experience, skill and knowledge which one gains in the experiments. Like long ago, when I used to build machines out of LEGO-Bricks, I destroyed my results soon after construction, because constructing was the most exciting and enriching part! (Of course, I would usually never destroy a Hologram.)

best regards,

Pianomaxx

Like long ago, when I used to build machines out of LEGO-Bricks, I destroyed my results soon after construction, because constructing was the most exciting and enriching part! (Of course, I would usually never destroy a Hologram.)

Yes, very true. I often try to live my life that way. Set a goal but make sure I enjoy the path and have fun with the path to the goal. That way if the goal is not reached I am still happy. If the goal is reached it is a bonus. Some people set the goal first and have a very bad time on the path to the goal. They may lose years trying to achive their goal. If the goal fails they are devistated. And even if the goal suceeds then they lost years being miserable trying to achive the goal. It always seemed better to try to enjoy the path first.

John

posts.author: MichaelH
posts.content_md:
> **Pianomaxx:** ...but I read that many holographers had problems in getting bright Denisyuks on PFG-01 in the beginning.

Piano, (may I call you Piano? ) I hadn't realized you were using PFG-01. That medium is a hard one to pull bright single-beam (which is what I presume you mean by Denisyuk) holograms out of. The dye in the emulsion absorbs a *lot* of light.

You can brighten them up quite a lot by adding mirrors and redirecting the spillover light back to the subject.
